args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (unhealthy, error rate ~18% across us-east, us-west, eu-west). v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. Rolled back checkout-api in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Follow-up: investigate root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and the service is healthy again. I also opened incident INC-0001 (SEV2), which paged on-call.

- **Before:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks with about an 18% error rate. Its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had also been unhealthy in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to that. It's now running in all three regions.
- **After:** the service reports healthy, with the error rate down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 says v2.3.1 caused the failures, describes the rollback and asks for the root cause to be found before v2.3.1 is deployed again. I created it at the same time as the final status check, so it doesn't say that the service has recovered. You may want to add that.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
